### Priority list
1. `canvas#chart` — the single largest rendered element (480×240, area 115200) and the whole visual point of the page; it's a bar chart drawn entirely by inline JS (`fillRect` calls), so pixel-perfect fidelity depends on getting that draw logic exactly right.
2. `#main > h1` — spans the full page width (1264×37) and is the only text content, so its exact wording and position are the next priority after the chart.

Since the canvas is painted by inline `<script>` that's fully visible in the page source (not opaque/cross-origin), I can copy that script verbatim rather than approximating it — this is the correct case to just transcribe, not flag as unrecreatable.

## Summary

This was an extremely minimal page: an `<h1>` heading and a single `<canvas id="chart">` bar chart, with no other markup or CSS.

**Key decision:** The canvas content is drawn entirely by inline JavaScript (`fillRect` calls plotting six bars from a hardcoded `values` array in `#017a07` green). Per the tooling guidance, a canvas painted by script normally has no DOM/CSS signal to extract — but here the drawing script itself was fully visible in the page source, not opaque or cross-origin. So rather than treating it as "unrecreatable," I copied the `<script>` block verbatim, which reproduces the chart's exact bars, widths, and color with certainty rather than approximation.

**Componentization:** None needed — two elements, no repeated structural fragments, so red-twine/windtailor weren't applicable here (no stylesheet or computed styling beyond the browser's default `<h1>` and one inline `fillStyle` color, both already captured verbatim).

**Fidelity check:** Screenshotted the original and the clone at the same 1280×900 viewport, ran odiff — result was `0` (exit code 0, 0% pixel difference), and a manual side-by-side image read confirmed the two renders are visually identical. No further iteration was needed.

Output written to `/var/folders/gb/m6478s0n5mx9wqlz8t_c03800000gn/T/gumshoe-agent-run-OOSry6/clone.html`. Screenshots (`original.png`, `clone-round1.png`, `diff-round1.png`) are saved in that same directory.
